## Disposition

**The original universal coloring question remains unresolved after approach 1 (1/5).** This draft publishes accepted partial results and the full independent AI written audit. It is neither a full proof nor a counterexample, adds no substantive approach and changes no turn count or queue file.

The target is a finite 6-regular, 6-uniform hypergraph with a three-coloring having at most three vertices of any color in each edge. Each edge has six distinct vertices; indexed edges may repeat. The report explicitly proves the equivalence of the multiplicity conventions and the maximum-degree-six formulation.

## Accepted mathematics and limits

The full written arguments establish the 36-copy regularization, pairing equivalence, potential and recoloring identities, the maximum-degree-three theorem, and the theorem for maximum degree six on at most eleven vertices. The report also retains the PG(2,5) two-or-three-points extraction obstruction and the limited direct symmetric Local Lemma calculation.

The displayed 15-vertex example has potential one and no strict improvement among 450 changes on at most two vertices; 52 moves are neutral. Its explicit three-vertex repair is a valid coloring. This is a non-strict local minimum for a particular method, not a counterexample to the target or a general repair theorem.

A separate precision note records the audit's clarification: the elementary and optimized symmetric Local Lemma sufficient thresholds differ, although both fail in this instance. The original report and audit remain complete and unchanged after additive edition notices.

## Evidence boundary

This is a ten-file authored prose-and-metadata edition under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004361/`. It contains no checker code, standalone computational fixtures, per-move files, result files, logs, datasets, copied source documents, private sources or private coordination material. No excluded code or fixture has been converted into new prose.

The 15-vertex edge list, initial coloring, histogram and three-vertex repair were already in the authored report and remain there. Historical auxiliary-file references and rerun commands remain in the full report and audit, but the leading notices state that those materials are omitted and the commands cannot be run from this edition. The PG(2,5) positive coloring vector and supplementary local-search witnesses are not included. Their checked properties are retained as historical audit observations; this draft does not claim that all finite-check evidence is reproducible from the included files.

The complete written reductions and restricted theorems do not depend on presenting finite tests as universal proof.

## Public sources and review

The target is Tibor Szabó's question in [Oberwolfach Report 1/2020, pp. 83–84](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46836?nt=1), also Problem 1 on page 13 of [Anastos–Lamaison–Steiner–Szabó, Majority Colorings of Sparse Digraphs](https://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/szabo/PDF/MajorityColorings.pdf). The subcubic result invokes [Brooks' theorem](https://doi.org/10.1017/S030500410002168X).

Two unchanged public-source metadata records preserve the original titles, public URLs, raw-PDF hashes and sizes, inspection history and limitations. Packaging is not a fresh source-reading or PDF-hashing pass. No novelty or comprehensive current-literature-status claim is made. The audit is independent AI review, not human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification.

## Integrity and repository scope

The original report body is 15,666 bytes, SHA-256 `da5d518f1182197e4d3766e5f2628c3c74315298e631c7130b7cc05795d86849`. The original audit body is 16,404 bytes, SHA-256 `a857f1fde059bd31b2ef191b5b666674d5d553f49fdce2d2d83e3a47f8c4dcfd`. Both remain exact contiguous suffixes after the new notices. The edition manifest binds all nine other files and lists itself without a self-hash.

Local manifest, exact-allowlist, UTF-8/JSON, link, addition-only patch and clean-replay checks passed. These checks establish packaging identity, not mathematical truth or reproduction of the omitted computations. No QUEUE.md or unrelated file is included. No CI-passing claim is made. Draft only; no merge, release or outside outreach.
